rationale: Round 0 built and passed, so the table is pushed moderately toward stronger obfuscation while respecting this profile: a small (2.8 KB text, 16 functions) FP-kernel benchmark (flops, fbench, whetstone, himeno) whose hot loops punish control-flow and branch overhead. SUB gets the highest DiversityGain weight because arithmetic substitution is nearly free at runtime and directly obscures the FP-heavy kernels; SPLIT and ICALL stay cheap-to-apply diversifiers (ICALL hides call targets in the richards scheduler/dispatch paths at low cost). FLA carries the highest SecurityGain since flattening the scheduler's dispatch loops (schedule, workfn, handlerfn) yields the best structural resistance, with RuntimeCost/SizeCost kept mid-range so it lands on the few large functions rather than every kernel. BCF is held at the lowest SecurityGain with high RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights because bogus predicates on tight FP loops would dominate the benchmark's measured runtime; IBR and IGV sit in the middle, adding indirection and data-hiding diversity without stacking branch overhead in the same hot blocks. All passes remain enabled since correctness was preserved with no ICE fallback.
